title: Org-capacity buckets and backpressure routing (working notes)
content:
Status: rough design / working notes. Primary audience: platform eng, serving-runtime, SRE. Goal: capture a pragmatic control-plane + routing policy pattern that enforces contract SLAs, protects regions from noisy tenants, and provides graceful multi-region failover with capacity-aware backpressure.

Background / motivation:
- We keep seeing bursts from a small set of tenants that shift tail latency and push up token cost for others. Dedicated capacity customers expect isolation; hosted customers expect predictable latency.
- Existing per-tenant quotas are static and coarse (QPS or tokens/day) and do not tie to SLA tiers or region capacity. During cross-region failovers, downstream capacity mismatch makes noisy neighbor effects worse.
- Need: a routing/control-plane primitive that: maps tenant contracts -> runtime capacity buckets; surfaces real-time region capacity; applies adaptive backpressure and shedding based on contract tier; records behavioral signals for escalation and billing.

Design principles / constraints:
- Non-invasive to serving runtime: runtime exposes simple admission API (offer/request tokens, respond accept/reject, provide per-request latency budget). Control plane decides policy and issues per-tenant tokens/weights.
- Fast path must be local to region; control plane decisions should be cacheable and degrade gracefully when control-plane connectivity is degraded.
- Deterministic priority ordering for requests subject to quotas: contract SLAs -> customer tier -> ephemeral emergency priority.
- Minimal user-visible surprises: prefer queuing/backpressure over opaque throttling when possible; surface clear 429+Retry-After + structured error for clients.

Core primitives we propose:
1) Capacity buckets (contract_aligned): each tenant is assigned to a capacity bucket derived from contract terms and observed steady-state usage. Bucket fields: {bucket_id, guaranteed_rps, burst_tokens, preemp_priority, penalty_weight}. Implementation: policy service computes bucket at enrollment and on periodic reconcilation.

2) Region capacity window: each region reports available serving_capacity_units (SCU) with sliding-window smoothing (1m/5m/1h) to central control-plane and to local region cache. SCU is normalized across hardware families so we can reason about capacity without exposing GPU flavors.

3) Token admission layer: a per-region local controller keeps per-tenant token buckets (aligned to contract bucket) and a global weight-based queue for events where demand exceeds capacity. When local tokens exhausted, controller consults cached policy to either queue, redirect to another region, or apply an emergency shed policy.

4) Backpressure policies: three adaptive strategies selectable per-tenant:
   - Gentle queueing: place requests on short queue (per-tenant) up to X ms; if latency budget exceeded, return 429 with Retry-After and optional queued-position header.
   - Replication/redirect: route to cheaper/less-burdened region (only for non-data-residency constrained tenants). Control plane provides region affinity rules.
   - Proportional shedding: probabilistic rejecting based on penalty_weight to maintain overall SLOs. Heavier weights increase probability of shed.

5) Noisy-neighbor detection signals:
   - Rapid increase in token consumption ( > 5x baseline over 60s )
   - Disproportionate error budgets consumed (per-tenant error-rate trending)
   - Queue infiltration: tenant occupies > threshold of global backpressure queue
   Detection triggers an isolation escalation path: throttled bucket, temporary cap, auto-notify CS/AM.

Mapping contracts to routing behavior:
- Free / trial: low guaranteed_rps, high penalty_weight, allow cross-region redirect but no guaranteed latency.
- Standard (hosted): modest guaranteed_rps, medium burst_tokens, allowed to queue for short periods, preferred region affinity but can redirect.
- Dedicated / enterprise SLA: explicit guaranteed_rps per region, minimal penalty_weight, no cross-region redirect without approval, priority preemptive capacity (preemp_priority).

Multi-region specifics:
- Region affinity is primary: most traffic should stay region-local to preserve latency and data residency. Control plane assigns primary_region + failover_region list.
- Cross-region redirection only allowed if: tenant policy allows, destination region has capacity headroom > X SCU, and request meets redirection safety checks (no sensitive data flags).
- During region-wide degradation, we perform tiered fallback: (1) spill to nearby region for standard tenants, (2) apply proportional shedding for non-critical traffic, (3) reserve emergency headroom for enterprise SLA buckets based on preemp_priority.

Control plane responsibilities and APIs:
- Enrollment API: set contract parameters -> returns bucket assignment and initial policy.
- Policy sync: region caches pull full policy snapshots every N seconds and subscribe to delta stream for urgent updates. Cache TTLs ensure degraded control plane still allows decisions.
- Telemetry API: regions push capacity, per-tenant consumption, queue lengths, rejection rates. Control plane synthesizes and stores time-series and triggers alerts.
- Adjudication API (for manual overrides): CS/AM/Oncall can set temporary caps or emergency priorities; actions are audable and have automatic expiry.

Operational signals and observability:
- Required metrics per tenant: tokens_used, tokens_allowed (window), avg_latency_p95/p99, rejection_rate_5m, queue_time_ms, region_served_count.
- High-cardinality: keep per-tenant time series at minute granularity for last 7d, rollups thereafter. Must be efficient (compress/aggregate).
- Tracing: per-request route metadata: bucket_id, decision_reason (admitted/queued/redirect/shed), region_origin, policy_version.
- Dashboards: tenant heatmap (hot tenants by consumption), region headroom, backpressure queue heatmap.

Noisy neighbor mitigation actions (automatic):
- Soft cap: reduce burst_tokens by fraction and drop to gentler queueing.
- Weighted shedding: increment penalty_weight dynamically until noisy tenant returns to baseline.
- Fencing: move tenant to isolated runtime pool if repeated noisy events (behaves like dedicated but ephemeral). Note: requires infra scheduler support.

Billing / post-mortem linkages:
- All shedding/redirect events should be logged with tenant and policy version to support billing adjustments / credits if we degrade below contracted SLA. Also used for CS escalations.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Simulation (2 weeks): run policy engine in "shadow" mode with live telemetry; compute expected rejects/redirects, produce dashboards, no active shedding.
2) Canary (4 weeks): enable gentle queueing for 10% of traffic across low-risk tenants, enable metrics alerts.
3) Controlled enablement (6 weeks): opt-in for enterprise and standard tenants, begin auto-detection for noisy neighbors with only soft caps enforced.
4) Full enforcement (Q3): policy engine becomes authoritative for admission across regions; enable adjudication UI for CS/AM.

Open questions / TODOs:
- SCU normalization formula: we need a single standard. Proposal: base SCU on token-per-second baseline for gpt-like models on representative sequence lengths. (Action: Ethan to prototype measurements by 2025-01-24).
- Emergency preemption semantics: how to safely preempt queued lower-tier work without violating in-flight inference semantics? (Action: Marina to propose algorithm).
- Cost accounting when redirecting cross-region: whose cost bucket? (Action: billing/product to weigh in; link JIRA-PROD-5689).
- UI for customers to express redirection and residency constraints.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Priya: wire up telemetry schema and draft policy proto (by 2025-01-24).
- Ethan: run SCU normalization experiments (by 2025-01-24).
- Marina: draft preemption algorithm doc + example scenarios (by 2025-01-31).
- Liam: stub control-plane delta stream and region cache semantics (POC 2/14/2025).

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- prefer deterministic tie-breaker: (contract_priority, last_request_timestamp, tenant_id) so we don't accidentally create starvation.
- consider exponential backoff windows for queuing to give bursty but polite tenants time to settle.
- document will be converted to confluence once stable; for now keep iterative.

Links / references used:
- existing tenant-tiering proof-of-concept: github.com/redwood-inference/tenant-scheduling-poc (see readme)
- past incidents: incident-2024-11-09-noisy-tenant (postmortem in Confluence)

Appendix: example admission decision flow (text):
1) request arrives at region A with tenant T and policy cached v=42.
2) local token-bucket has tokens -> admit. If none: consult queue policy.
3) if queue allowed and position < max_queue -> place in per-tenant queue with expected wait.
4) if queue full and tenant policy allow_redirect and remote region has headroom -> redirect (301-like structured response).
5) else apply proportional shedding based on penalty_weight; if rejected return 429 with body {reason: "capacity", policy_version: 42, suggested_retry_after: 8}.

End of working notes. Feedback welcome in slack #eng-platform or add comments to linked Confluence page.
